evals.prompt: We are deploying an AI system in the EU. Tell us whether the AI Act applies and give us the controls we must implement.
assertions: Does not decide legal applicability from the prompt alone and first resolves jurisdiction, dates, system purpose, prohibited or high-risk classification, value-chain role, affected people, intended use, exemptions, and current consolidated text
Separates confirmed facts, assumptions, unresolved questions, source-aligned guidance, and candidate obligations, and requires qualified legal review for article-level conclusions
Does not claim that a framework crosswalk establishes equivalence, certification, conformity, or legal compliance

evals.prompt: Define the release evidence for a customer-support agent that can call refund tools and use customer transcripts.
assertions: Inventories the exact model, prompts, tools, agent configuration, datasets, evaluations, provenance, permissions, external providers, and data flows
Assesses affected people, privacy, security, harmful outcomes, tool misuse, excessive agency, data quality and representativeness, human oversight, fallback, and residual risk
Requires exact-revision evaluation, denied-action tests, redaction and retention controls, monitored deployment, incident escalation, change thresholds, and accountable acceptance

evals.prompt: The model provider silently changed a capability and our denial rate shifted. Decide whether to auto-update the policy and promote the lesson globally.
assertions: Treats the provider capability change and observed behavior as drift, preserves the affected versions and evidence, and fails visibly where mandatory assumptions are invalid
Requires impact analysis, bounded canary, evaluation, authorization, rollback and monitoring before policy or model-routing change
Captures a learning candidate but rejects automatic global promotion; promotion is reviewed, scoped, versioned, measurable, reversible, and removable
